incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended; ss. 5-14 (incorporation and articles), ss. 19-21 (directors), ss. 42-50 (registered office and corporate records), ss. 104-106 (by-laws and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (filed electronically via the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; shares may be issued for such consideration as fixed by the directors. No escrow account obligation is imposed by the CBCA for ordinary private corporations; escrow-type restrictions apply only to specified regulated issuers, which does not apply to this consulting entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscription for 100 Class A common shares, as set forth in the subscription agreement, is approved and accepted; the Chief Executive Officer shall issue the shares on full receipt of agreed consideration; and [ADDRESS] is adopted as the registered office of the Corporation, with the registered agent authorized to accept service. FURTHER RESOLVED that [NAME] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] Corporate Secretary. All lawful acts of directors and officers implementing these resolutions are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada - Online Name Reservation and NUANS Search Portal (corporateonline.ised-isde.canada.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search against the proposed corporate name through the Corporations Canada online portal or an accredited NUANS search house. Select a name that is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing corporate names or trademarks. Reserve the approved name for 90 days and obtain the official name reservation number to be cited in the Articles of Incorporation. For expedited formation, a numbered company may be adopted without reservation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended list of three alternates and re-run the NUANS search within the same reservation window, or proceed with a numbered company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, ISED - Online Filing Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation on the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, entering the proposed name or reservation number, the share structure, the maximum number of shares, the number of directors, the first directors' names, and the registered office address. Pay the statutory filing fee of CAD 200 by credit card. For online filings, the certificate of incorporation is issued immediately after data verification passes.
required_dossiers: NUANS name reservation certificate (if named company)
Consent to act as first director (s. 6 CBCA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for completeness or name issues, correct the flagged fields and resubmit the amended articles; a fresh filing number may be required, and the previous fee is credited or forfeited according to Corporations Canada refund policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of the registration of the articles, submit Form 3 - Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors, identifying the registered office address and the names of the first directors. The registered office must remain within Canada in the province specified in the articles.
required_dossiers: Form 3 - Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings may be submitted online with an explanatory note; continued non-compliance beyond 15 days exposes the corporation to late-filing penalties and potential dissolution proceedings under the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the first board meeting, adopt the general operating by-law pursuant to subsection 104(1) of the CBCA, confirm the share issuance and officer appointments, approve the corporate minute book, adopt a banking resolution, and ratify the registered agent engagement. Issue share certificates reflecting the Class A common share subscription.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice of first board meeting
Share certificate stubs and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder challenges by-law validity for procedural defects, call a conforming shareholders' meeting to confirm or ratify the by-law at the next annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Registrations with Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation's Business Number (BN) at the CRA Business Registration Online service. Elect to register for the GST/HST account (required when annual worldwide taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000) and open payroll and corporate income tax accounts. The corporate income tax account is normally created automatically upon incorporation; separate registration is required for GST/HST and payroll.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and directors' details
Expected revenue and business activity description (ISIC 7490)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected or the BN is not issued, contact the CRA Business Registration line (1-800-959-5525) to verify corporate identity and re-submit the registration using the CRA corporate access number found on the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial corporate registry of the province of operation (e.g., ServiceOntario for Ontario, Registraire des entreprises for Quebec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the federal corporation carries on business in a province other than the registered office province, file an extra-provincial registration with the applicable provincial registry within the prescribed period (generally 30 days after commencing business). Provide the certificate of incorporation and, where required, the name of a local attorney for service of process.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the federal certificate of incorporation
Extra-provincial registration form of the host province
Notice of Registered Office and Directors (Form 3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A late registration is cured by filing the outstanding declaration and paying the provincial late fee; the corporation's right to commence legal proceedings in provincial courts is suspended pending compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational, Physical and Office Licensing Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial occupational health and safety regulator (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development) and municipal building/fire department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the leased professional office occupied by the regulatory consultancy, obtain a municipal occupancy/fire-safety certificate evidencing compliance with the applicable fire code and building occupancy limits. Register the workplace with the provincial occupational health and safety authority where required and post the required health-and-safety notices. As the business is a non-manufacturing consultancy, no industrial process license or environmental discharge permit is required.
required_dossiers: Building lease and municipal zoning compliance letter
Occupational health and safety registration (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect is identified in a fire safety inspection, remedy the flagged non-compliance and request a re-inspection; interim approval may be obtained by filing a written corrective action plan with the municipal fire marshal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the undertaking is a non-manufacturing professional services firm (ISIC 7490); no industrial licensing board authorization is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required; general municipal zoning and occupancy approval suffices for the office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and provincial environmental regulator - not applicable to office-based consulting activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based activity with no specified industrial undertaking; no EIA screening or registration required under the Impact Assessment Act, 2019.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated; the office must comply with municipal sewer and waste disposal by-laws, the Canada Occupational Health and Safety Regulations for indoor air, and applicable building mechanical code standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and building occupancy inspection by the municipal fire marshal and building department; occupancy load and egress compliance; first-aid and emergency evacuation plans per the applicable provincial fire code; occupational health and safety clearance under the Canada Labour Code Part II or the applicable provincial OHS statute.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC); online portal: My Business Account (CRA) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada must obtain a Business Number (BN) from CRA by using Business Registration Online (BRO) or filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number). CRA issues a 9-digit BN which is then activated for the Income Tax program account (RC####) and, where applicable, the GST/HST program account (RT####). Foreign-incorporated entities must provide proof of incorporation, registered office address, Canadian agent or representative details, and, if carrying on a taxable business, complete the T2 corporate income tax registration procedures. The BN serves as the corporate TIN and as the GST/HST registration number; Canada does not maintain a separate VAT identification numbering system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box or elective pass-through classification for business corporations. A federal corporation is subject to entity-level tax under Part I of the Income Tax Act as a resident or non-resident corporation. Limited statutory elections include the section 216(1) election for a non-resident corporation to compute Canadian rental income on a net basis and the section 98(6) partnership continuation election in eligible reorganizations. Hybrid mismatch consequences are governed by Income Tax Act sections 18.2 and 18.3, and no optional classification election is available for GST/HST.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable revenues (including zero-rated supplies) over any four consecutive calendar quarters under Excise Tax Act section 148; non-residents supplying taxable goods or services in Canada are subject to the same threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based invoice stamping, or government authentication of electronic invoices. Businesses may issue electronic invoices, and CRA requires GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies above CAD 10,000 to file returns electronically (GST34) in most cases. Exported supply documentation must be retained in a readable electronic or paper format, and CRA may electronically audit records using the authorized GST/HST record layout requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, goods exported by the supplier or delivered outside Canada are zero-rated when the supplier maintains contemporaneous proof of export. Services supplied to a non-resident person, including medical device regulatory consulting services, are zero-rated if the non-resident is not registered under the GST/HST system and the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at all times the service is performed. The supplier must obtain and retain documentary evidence establishing the non-resident status of the recipient and delivery of the service to that non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration submitted to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES) when the export value exceeds CAD 2,000
Bill of lading, air waybill or combined transport document evidencing shipment from Canada for goods
Commercial invoice describing the medical device regulatory consulting service or exported goods and identifying the non-resident counterparty
Bank wire confirmation or foreign currency receipt showing receipt of consideration from the non-resident customer
CBSA cargo control document, freight forwarder certificate, courier tracking record, or service completion report evidencing offshore delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period, extended indefinitely where the exporter has misrepresented facts or committed fraud. If export zero-rating is not substantiated, CRA will assess uncollected GST or HST at the applicable rate, plus daily compound interest and penalties. Late filing penalties for GST/HST returns amount to 3% of the balance owing plus an additional 1% for each complete month, to a maximum of 12 months. False claims of export zero-rating made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence attract an additional 5% penalty on the understated tax; willful evasion can result in fines of up to CAD 25,000 and/or imprisonment under Excise Tax Act sections 327 and 328. CRA will also claw back input tax credits that were claimed in respect of non-qualifying or unsupported supplies and may apply prosecution to repeat offenders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential regulation of deposit-taking institutions by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act; anti-money-laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility as an IMF Article VIII member. There is no foreign-exchange-control legislation, no prior approval requirement for inward investment, and no restriction on the repatriation of dividends, branch profits, or capital by non-resident shareholders of a corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA). Service-export revenue from FDA 510(k) and European CE Mark consulting may be received and held in CAD, USD, or EUR without conversion mandate. The only residual frictions are non-treaty Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%; generally reduced to 5% on dividends and 0-15% on interest/royalties under an applicable tax treaty) and FINTRAC reporting by the receiving financial institution of international electronic fund transfers (EFTs) equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline, minimum conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export or service-export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely in domestic or offshore accounts. The only compliance duty is passive: financial institutions must report international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and the corporate client must supply accurate remittance purpose narratives when requested. The Export Development Canada (EDC) framework supports exporters voluntarily but imposes no surrender directives.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with material legal constraints. A non-resident digital EMI (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer) may lawfully service a Canadian corporate client, but any EMI carrying on money-services business in Canada must be registered with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business (MSB) under the PCMLTFA; unregistered offshore EMIs cannot clear CAD through Payments Canada and typically route through pooled omnibus accounts that do not constitute 'deposits' protected under the Bank Act or eligible for CDIC insurance. EMIs are suitable only for low-value fee intake and small vendor disbursements, not for escrow of client regulatory fees or high-value SWIFT treasury flows. A Tier-1 chartered bank account remains the legally required anchor for capital injections and multi-currency clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for a CBCA corporation under the PCMLTFA non-face-to-face verification regime (sections 63-64 of the Regulations), provided identity evidence for directors and beneficial owners is obtained from independent, reliable third-party sources, or a combination of certified incorporation documents, passport/government-issued ID, and a corporate registry search. Physical attendance at a branch is not statutorily mandated for Canadian-resident directors; however, non-resident directors should expect bank-level policy requiring in-person verification at a Canadian branch, or remote verification with notarized/legalized identity documents and an enhanced source-of-funds questionnaire. In practice, a fully remote end-to-end opening is achievable for a federally incorporated consulting company within 5-10 business days when there is a Canadian registered office, a Canadian-resident signatory, and clean sanctions screening; physical attendance materially shortens escalation and increases approval probability for escrow-linked accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director/UBO structure and anticipated cross-border equity injection exceeding CAD 100,000 on account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBCA certificate of incorporation and full bylaws; directors'/shareholders' resolutions; registered-office certificate; UBO schedule with date of birth and residential address; passport/government-issued ID for every director and 20%+ beneficial owner; share subscription agreement with proof of funding source (bank statement of subscribing shareholder); CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; corporate registry search printout confirming active status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound wires from US medical-device sponsors or EU notified bodies for FDA 510(k)/CE consulting fees, triggering revenue-profile mismatch review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements and project-specific consulting contracts naming the Canadian entity as service provider; itemized invoices and payment schedules; evidence of deliverable transmission (510(k) submission packages, clinical-evaluation reports, CE technical files); ISIC 7490 scope statement on company letterhead; client company confirmations; bank statements of prior revenue cycles demonstrating recurring fee pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of third-party client funds to be remitted onward as FDA user fees or notified-body filing fees, raising deposit-taking and MSB classification concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming the entity does not engage in 'deposit' business within the meaning of the Bank Act and is not required to be an MSB; escrow/agency agreement with the client; transparent ledger of pass-through payments; contractual flow-of-funds clause; invoices from the FDA (user-fee form 5174) and notified bodies made out to the clinical sponsor rather than to the consulting entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name or date-of-birth similarity between a director and a sanctions-list or politically exposed person (PEP), or a jurisdictional flag from a EU/US client footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening clarity package: citizenship and residency evidence; negative confirmation against OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated, EU, and Canadian autonomous sanctions lists; short professional biography; explanation of any transliteration variations; PEP status declaration; proposed remedial monitoring arrangement presented to the compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For share capital or shareholder loan injections, route a SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the Canadian bank's clearing account (USD via the bank's New York/Chicago correspondent and internal journal into the CAD operating account, or direct CAD through a Lynx participant). The remittance narrative must state a clean purpose descriptor: 'Share capital contribution' or 'Intercompany loan', referencing the subscription or loan agreement number and date. FINTRAC requires the receiving Canadian financial institution to report international EFTs ≥ CAD 10,000; the corporate client is not independently obligated to file, but must answer source-of-wealth requests within 48 hours. CAD funds become immediately available after clearing; no Bank of Canada approval or surrender-timeframe constraint applies. Note that a shareholder loan from a non-resident may incidentally trigger Form T106 reporting for transfer-pricing and Part XIII purposes, which is a tax-compliance matter outside the banking onboarding gate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border USD/EUR vendor payments or refunds; (2) Payments Canada Lynx real-time gross settlement for same-day CAD payments; (3) commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) for equipment purchase or subcontractor payments — permissible but disproportionate for advisory-only disbursements; (4) cross-border ACH through EFT/Paynet for recurring US subscriptions, and SEPA euro transfers through the bank's European correspondent. To avoid OFAC/sanctions false positives, include exact beneficiary legal name, full address, ISO 20022 structured remittance information, and the underlying contract reference. Settlement finality is achieved on debit/credit of the correspondent account rather than on initiation; fund availability should be tested before committing milestone payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) concluded with Tier-1 Canadian banks under an ISDA master agreement, with tenors up to 24 months to lock consulting-fee conversion rates.
Vanilla OTC currency options (call/put) and zero-cost collars for asymmetric protection of large USD/EUR fee receipts.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) for balance-sheet hedging of intercompany loans or deferred milestone receivables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): generally neither available nor necessary for CAD because CAD is fully convertible and actively traded onshore and offshore; NDFs are permissible only for odd-lot exposures in restricted currencies arising from sub-accounts, and require additional capital treatment under OSFI guidance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal corporate income tax (general rate, post-2012 reduction).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for CCPCs); investment tax credits (SR&ED, qualified property); 10% federal investment tax credit for certain clean-tech assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return / CRA e-File and Netfile for registered tax preparers; commercial software mandatory for e-filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due no later than six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance-due payments due two months for non-CCPCs and three months for CCPCs after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross commercial revenues from all sources, including consulting fees from FDA/CE regulatory projects.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source revenues; foreign-source revenues to be allocable only under treaty attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after expense deductions and loss claims; recapture of prior-year capital cost allowance if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Form T2121 if carrying on business with a permanent establishment structure; otherwise report as Part XIV non-resident taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate income tax payable, after small business deduction and other credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty credits via Form T2209/Form T2036; attach proof of foreign tax paid or deemed paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Controlled transaction disclosure and transfer-pricing documentation checklist.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File T106 for any reportable transaction with a non-arm's-length non-resident exceeding CAD 100,000 in aggregate annual value.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax for repeat failure; statutory interest compounds daily on unpaid balances (Canada Revenue Agency prescribed rate, currently 9%+ per annum).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident recipient must obtain a Canadian Form NR302/NR303 or a signed Certificate of Residency (Form T2203 cross-reference) from their domestic tax authority; submit a waiver or reduced-withholding application to CRA before payment; recipient claims treaty relief at source by using the Canada withholding tax agreement schedule; payer must retain supporting TRC evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties to non-residents: 25% statutory, reduced to 10% under most DTA (0% for pure copyright or software where beneficial owner is an approved peer). Interest to non-residents: 25% statutory, typically 0% under Canada–US Treaty and 10% under Canada–EU DTA; domestic exemption applies to arm's-length interest paid to unrelated creditors.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous TP documentation trigger: controlled non-resident transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate annual value; T106 mandatory for individual transactions > CAD 100,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in Canada; substance is tested under GAAR (section 245 Income Tax Act), treaty shopping abuse analysis, and CRA administrative practice requiring beneficial ownership, real management, and commercial risk assumption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of consulting revenue, provision of fake expense invoices, or deliberate misallocation of revenue to offshore shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 238 and 239 Income Tax Act: fine up to 200% of evaded tax + civil penalties (50% gross negligence penalty); additional civil liability for interest compounding daily.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid withholding amounts (s.227.1 ITA) and for any CPCA/Excise Act liabilities; criminal conviction may impose imprisonment up to 5 years in addition to restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance Claiming Treaty Benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Canadian corporation used solely as an invoicing pass-through without directors, employees, bank accounts, physical office, or real operational decision-making, while self-certifying treaty LOB eligibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief under s.245 GAAR; withholding tax recollected at 25%; penalty up to CAD 10,000 per false statement under s.162(6); reassessment of sham transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under s.245(3): directors jointly and severally liable for taxes that would have been payable absent the GAAR; travel bans and asset freezes may occur under criminal AML proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML – Unreported Beneficial Ownership and Wire Transparency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register beneficial ownership in FINTRAC / corporate registry; using layered shell companies for cross-border FDA/CE fee payments without documenting economic substance; accepting overpayments without a written commercial contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: administrative monetary penalty up to CAD 500,000 for individuals and up to CAD 1,000,000 for entities; criminal fine and imprisonment up to 5 years for directors found guilty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted personally for authorizing, permitting, or acquiescing in money-laundering activity (s.83.08 Criminal Code); personal bank accounts may be frozen via civil forfeiture orders, with mandatory reporting to FINTRAC for any cross-border transfer > CAD 10,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Corporate Violation – Fraudulent Certification for FDA/CE Support Work
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing false regulatory test results, fabricated ISO confirmation, or backdated Certificates of Compliance in a regulatory consulting engagement, causing client regulatory non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Criminal Code s.380 (fraud), indictable offence with imprisonment up to 14 years; additional penalties under the Food and Drugs Act for false declarations; possible debarment from federal procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for fraudulent misrepresentations under common law; in addition to restitution to harmed parties, travel bans and extradition may proceed from Canada due to treaty obligations.
